newsitem.title: USA: Ok. City bomb defendants to be tried separately.
newsitem.headline: Ok. City bomb defendants to be tried separately.

text.p: The judge in the Oklahoma City bombing trial on Friday ordered separate trials for the two defendants, saying it was the only way to provide a fair hearing for both men.
The judge also ordered that Timothy McVeigh be tried before co-defendant Terry Nichols.

U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch, in a 20-page decision, said "a joint trial of these defendants presents such an unacceptable risk of prejudice to both of them as to require separate trials."
Former Army buddies McVeigh and Nichols are accused of the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people and injured about 500.
Both defendants urged the judge to grant separate trials because, they said, their defenses would be based in part on pointing the finger of blame at each other.
Trial dates have not been set. Prosecutors had opposed the defense motion for separate trials, saying that trying the two men together would provide a jury with a full picture of the crime.
